result.topic_en: Riemann rewrites the minimal-surface equations using the variables X and X' (combinations of x and (x)i), concludes that η depends only on X and η' only on X', and then fixes the constants of the Möbius transformation η₁ = c(α−η)/(1+αη) from the values at η = 0 and η = ∞, finding |c| = 1, c = e^{θi}.
result.transcription:
[?]Ich sehe aber, daß ich in den spätern Formeln $x-ti$ oder
$x+(x)i = 2X$ gesetzt habe. Die Rechnung ist also folgende
$2\,ds - \eta(dx + d(x)i) + \frac{r}{\eta'}(dx - d(x)i) = 0$
$2\,ds' + \frac{1}{\eta}(dx + d(x)i) - \eta'(dx - d(x)i) = 0$
oder, $x + (x)i = 2X$, $x - (x)i = 2X'$ gesetzt
$ds - \eta\,dX + \frac{1}{\eta'}dX' = 0$, also $\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial X'} = \frac{1}{\eta\eta'}\frac{\partial\eta'}{\partial X}$
$ds' + \frac{1}{\eta}dX - \eta' dX' = 0$, also $\frac{1}{\eta\eta'}\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial X'} = \frac{\partial\eta'}{\partial X}$
$C^x$ $\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial X'} = 0$, $\frac{\partial\eta'}{\partial X} = 0$, $\eta$ f. v. $X$, $\eta'$ v. $X'$
$ds - \eta\frac{\partial X}{\partial\eta}\partial\eta + \frac{1}{\eta'}\frac{\partial X'}{\partial\eta'}\partial\eta' = 0$
$ds' + \frac{1}{\eta}\frac{\partial X}{\partial\eta}\partial\eta - \eta'\frac{\partial X'}{\partial\eta'}\partial\eta' = 0$
Da $x = X + X'$, $\frac{\partial X}{\partial\eta'} = 0$, $\frac{\partial X'}{\partial\eta} = 0$, so ist $\frac{\partial x}{\partial\eta} = \frac{\partial X}{\partial\eta}$
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial\eta'} = \frac{\partial X'}{\partial\eta'}$. $x = \int\frac{\partial x}{\partial\eta}\partial\eta + \int\frac{\partial x}{\partial\eta'}\partial\eta' = X + X'$

Die Constante in $\eta_1 = [-\alpha-]\, c\,\frac{\alpha - \eta}{1+\alpha\eta}$
wird durch die Werthe [-Coefficient-] {+Ausdruck+} welche $\eta_1$
für $\eta = 0$ u. $\eta = \infty$ annimmt.
für $\eta = 0$ ; $\eta_1 = \beta$, so ist [-f-] für $\eta = \infty$
[?]u. für $\eta = 0$ ; $\eta_1 = \beta_1$ so ist für $\eta = \infty$
$\eta_1 = -\frac{1}{\beta'}$ nun ergiebt sich
[-nun wird also [?]-]
$\beta = +c\alpha$ $\mp\frac{1}{\beta'} = \frac{c}{\alpha'}$, folglich
$\beta = \mp\frac{\alpha}{c'}$, also $cc' = 1$ oder der Modul
von $c = 1$. $c = e^{\theta i}$

methods.what: Change to complex variables X, X' turning the minimal-surface system into one in X and X'
η is a function of X alone and η' of X' alone (holomorphy condition)
Decomposition of x as the sum of integrals over η and η'
Determination of the constant of the Möbius transformation from the values at 0 and ∞; the constant has modulus 1

items.english: If θ is taken different from zero, then evidently in the coordinate transformations one only has to multiply η₁ and η'₁ by e^{θi}, e^{−θi}; otherwise everything remains unchanged.
